About me

I work on robotic perception and manipulation, with a particular interest in how robots can use vision, sensing and learning to interact with the physical world. My research spans medical robotics, precision assembly and robotic disassembly.

I am an Assistant Professor in Robotics and Computer Vision at Heriot-Watt University, within the Institute of Signals, Sensors and Systems in the School of Engineering and Physical Sciences, and a member of the National Robotarium. I co-lead ARM²Lab with Dr Ignacio Carlucho.

I am Co-Director of the CDT in Dependable and Deployable AI for Robotics (D2AIR) and Deputy Postgraduate Research (PGR) Coordinator in the School of Engineering and Physical Sciences. I also coordinate Heriot-Watt’s PhD partnerships with Xidian University and Ocean University.

Before joining Heriot-Watt, I was a postdoctoral researcher in the Biomedical Robotics Laboratory at the Italian Institute of Technology. I completed my PhD at the University of Crete, studying learning from demonstration for robotic manipulation.

Research interests

Vision-guided manipulation, multimodal sensing, learning from demonstration, and precision robotic intervention in healthcare and manufacturing.

Research

Perception into action.

Enabling robots to sense, learn and manipulate in demanding environments.

Medical robotics

I investigate vision-guided robotic interventions in soft tissues, bringing together ultrasound, robotic control and multimodal sensing. I am interested in how complementary sensory information can support precise needle placement and more dependable interaction with deformable environments.

Precision manipulation and assembly

My work explores robotic handling and alignment of delicate components, including optical assembly. Combining the reach of a robot arm with fine local motion provides a route towards more dexterous manipulation and precise placement.

Robotic disassembly and learning

I study adaptive manipulation for the disassembly of electronic devices, including dual-arm coordination, visual recognition and task planning. A central interest is how robots can use prior experience and new observations to adapt to unfamiliar objects and changing tasks.

Earlier projects

Earlier work includes ANASA, on robotic sorting of recyclable materials; ENTIMENT, on temporal cognition for commercial robots; TIMESTORM, on the temporal aspects of human–machine interaction; and METR, on mental training in artificial agents.

For current projects, the research team and lab demonstrations, visit ARM²Lab ↗.

Teaching & supervision

Learning by doing.

Connecting the foundations of vision and robotics with practical systems.

Machine Vision B31MV · MSc

SemesterSpring · every year
Lectures3 hours per week
Labs2 hours per week

B31MV takes a relatively high-level, vision-systems perspective, with an emphasis on how images are used for perception, learning and decision-making, rather than focusing heavily on the underlying signal-processing theory.

Open Canvas ↗ for course materials, announcements and timetable information (Heriot-Watt login required).

Weekly outline

WeekTopics
1Introduction to human, machine, computer and robotic vision, with relevant applications.
2Image formation: camera models, projections and image representations.
3Basic image processing: convolution, filtering, segmentation, edge detection and image interpolation.
4Feature extraction and matching; feature detectors and descriptors; K-means clustering; visual codebooks and Bag of Visual Words; applications to object detection, image classification and visual search.
5Supervised learning, training/validation/test splits, linear regression and regularisation.
6Consolidation Week (Learning Break)
7Neural networks and convolutional neural networks.
83D vision, camera calibration and stereo triangulation.
9Structured light, structure from motion and photometric stereo.
10RANSAC, Hough transforms, visual servoing and robotics.
11–12Revision and practice, including mock exams.
Syllabus & learning activities
Learning activityDetailsLearning outcomes
Lectures
  • Introduction: human, machine, computer and robotic vision, and applications.
  • Image formation: camera models, projections and image representations.
  • Basic image processing: convolution, filtering, segmentation, edge detection and image interpolation.
  • Feature extraction and matching: feature detectors and descriptors; unsupervised clustering (K-means); visual codebooks; Bag of Visual Words; applications to object detection, image classification and visual search.
  • 3D imaging: applications, laser and stereo triangulation, structured light, structure from motion and photometric stereo.
  • Visual servoing and applications of vision for robotic control.
  • Tracking: templates and cross-correlation; blob trackers.
  • Machine learning: deep learning models for image/video recognition and classification, data preparation and model validation.
1, 2, 3, 4, 5
Tutorials and labs
  • Visual servoing and applications of vision for robotic control.
  • Tracking: templates and cross-correlation; blob trackers.
  • Machine learning: deep learning models for image/video recognition and classification, data preparation and model validation.
1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7

MSc projects Project ideas & student supervision

I am always happy to welcome students who are curious about robotics and computer vision. Working with students is one of the parts of my job I enjoy most. I am passionate about helping them develop their ideas, build confidence in research and produce a high-quality thesis they can be proud of.

If one of these ideas interests you, or you have a project of your own in mind, please get in touch. We can shape the scope around your interests and experience.

Example MSc project ideas

Ultrasound perception for robotic needle interventions

Develop and evaluate an image-analysis method to identify tissue targets and safe access regions in ultrasound images. Compare segmentation methods and study temporal consistency across image sequences.

Python · computer vision · medical robotics

Learning robotic disassembly from instructional videos

Use visual models to extract components and task steps from disassembly videos, then build a structured plan for a robot. Evaluate how well the approach transfers to unfamiliar electronic devices.

Python · vision-language models · task planning

Vision-guided precision optical assembly

Develop a camera-based alignment method for delicate components using a macro–micro robotic system. Compare positioning accuracy and placement success with and without visual feedback.

Computer vision · robot control · precision manipulation

Robotic handling of transparent and flexible objects

Investigate how a robot can detect and grasp transparent bags or deformable packaging. Compare perception and grasp-selection approaches under changing backgrounds, lighting and object shapes.

Computer vision · machine learning · robotic grasping
